answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a proof-of-stake bond that every new identity must lock before it can vote or earn. A single fake agent is cheap, so sybils mass-produce them; but if each identity must post a bond that is slashed when misbehavior is proven, a thousand clones need a thousand locked stakes. That turns a free flood into a crippling expense. The honest swarm survives, like a comet steering past an island while a dead lagoon of clones drowns in its own collateral.
